citations.A1: the cache is loaded once and has no invalidation — `if _cache is None` is the only condition that ever reads the file, so after the first call nothing on disk can trigger a reload; fix by storing the file's identity (`os.stat` → `st_mtime_ns`, `st_size`, `st_ino`/`st_dev`) alongside the parsed data and re-stat'ing on every call
citations.A2: Not a fix — a TTL / periodic expiry: it only shortens the staleness window, still serves stale values for up to the TTL
citations.A3: Not a fix — an explicit `reload_config()` for callers to call: correctness now depends on every call site remembering, which is the same failure with more surface.
citations.A4: the cache ignores `path`, so the first caller's file is returned to every later caller regardless of the path they pass; fix by keying the cache dict on the resolved absolute path
citations.A6: Returning the shared mutable dict lets any caller's mutation silently become everyone's config ... fix by returning a deep copy or an immutable view.
citations.A7: write `{"v":1}` to `config.json`, call `get_config()`, overwrite the file with `{"v":2}`, call `get_config()` again in the same process — it returns `v=1`. Fix is proven when the second call returns `v=2`
